items.title: Committee established
items.description: The Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee was formally established as a united non-profit body representing legally registered Chinese associations in Queensland, dedicated to dialogue with federal, state, and local government.

items.description: The official launch was held at Tattersall's Club in Brisbane, bringing together member organisations and community representatives to mark a new chapter for the Chinese community in Queensland.

members.name: Peter Zhuang
members.bio:
Chairman of the Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee.
Represents the Chinese community in dialogue with federal, state, and local government.

members.name: Chen Yimin
members.bio:
President of Universal Education & Multicultural Exchange Association Inc. (UEMEA).
Originally from China, Alan Chen came to Australia in 1990 and has actively supported local multicultural community events, promoting a vibrant, harmonious, and diverse society.

members.name: Chen Fan
members.bio:
President of Mainland Chinese Society Queensland.
Recipient of the Centenary Medal of Federation of Australia and the 2001 International Year of Volunteers award. He has long supported Chinese arts, cultural exchange, and multicultural community development in Queensland.

members.name: He Ying
members.bio:
Australian lawyer.
An ANU law honours graduate with more than 12 years of legal practice experience, leading a professional legal team serving Australian and international clients. She founded the Australia-Asia Women's Association, served as the 28th President of the Brisbane Chinese Lions Club, and actively supports multicultural exchange, community service, and social inclusion.

members.name: Rebecca Zhang
members.bio:
Qualified CPA.
With 15+ years' experience across multiple industries, Rebecca is currently a Finance Manager with strong expertise in financial reporting, budgeting, and business advisory. She is the founder of Risenco, providing VCFO and finance support services to SMEs.

events.title: Community activities
events.description: Explore the committee’s work in community service, cultural exchange and government engagement, through activities shared by our members and the wider community.

items.title: Community stroke awareness talk
items.description:
On 18 June 2026, the Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee joined the Queensland Chinese Doctors Association to host a community stroke awareness talk at Runcorn Tavern.

Michael Doohan presented the session, with interpreting by Dr Anna Liu, Secretary of the Queensland Chinese Doctors Association. The talk covered early signs of stroke, emergency response and prevention. Both speakers answered questions and spoke with participants after the presentation.

The event was exclusively sponsored by 1st Care Community.

items.title: Delegation meets Queensland Multiculturalism Minister Fiona Simpson MP
items.description:
On the morning of 17 June 2026, Chairman Peter Zhuang led an eight-member Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee delegation to meet Multiculturalism Minister Fiona Simpson MP at the Queensland Government building.

The delegation introduced the committee’s purpose, development and member organisations’ community work. Discussions covered communication between government and the Chinese community, participation in public affairs and multicultural development. The Minister acknowledged the Chinese community’s contribution to Queensland’s economy, society and culture.

Staff accompanied the delegation on a tour of the building after the meeting, which strengthened the committee’s connections with the State Government.

items.title: Australian family law seminar
items.description:
On the afternoon of 16 May 2026, the Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee hosted an Australian family law seminar at Runcorn Tavern, presented by Vice-Chair Chai Hoe of Harmony Legal.

The session covered the importance of wills, property division and personal asset protection in divorce, and children’s future and family financial security. Chai Hoe answered questions and discussed these topics with participants after the presentation.

The committee thanks Vice-Chair Alan Chen for sponsoring the venue.

items.title: Meeting with Brisbane Lord Mayor Adrian Schrinner
items.description:
On 5 May 2026, Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee member representatives visited Brisbane City Hall to meet Lord Mayor Adrian Schrinner and his team. Nathan Percy, Director of City Business for the Lord Mayor, and adviser Eddie Stephens also attended.

Chairman Peter Zhuang introduced the committee’s background, purpose and development. Members introduced their organisations and discussed shared community interests with the Lord Mayor.

Mr Zhuang made a donation to the Lord Mayor’s Charitable Trust on behalf of Deputy Secretary-General Joe Zhao. The committee also presented a commemorative gift, and participants took a group photo to mark the exchange between the community and local government.

items.title: Visit to the Queensland Holocaust Museum
items.description:
On 26 April 2026, Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee member representatives visited the Queensland Holocaust Museum. Committee adviser Michael Choi OAM initiated and coordinated the visit and sponsored admission.

Museum Director Jason Steinberg welcomed the group. Michael Choi OAM shared the history of Shanghai’s reception of Jewish refugees during the Second World War. Guided by Toni and Jason, members explored the exhibitions and arranged pebbles into the Chinese character Hua in remembrance of Holocaust survivors who had passed away.

Chairman Peter Zhuang thanked the hosts and presented a commemorative gift. Joe Zhao donated A$188 to support the museum. The visit encouraged historical understanding and cultural exchange.

items.title: Visit to the Chinese Australian war memorial
items.description:
At 3:30 pm on 12 April 2026, more than 30 representatives from Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee member organisations visited the Chinese Australian war memorial at Sunnybank RSL.

Lewis Lee OAM hosted the event. Harry Claasen OAM introduced the history of Sunnybank RSL, and Lewis Lee OAM spoke about Chinese Australian military service and the establishment of the memorial. Participants offered candles in tribute. Parnam Singh Heir also introduced the Indian Australian war memorial.

Chairman Peter Zhuang thanked the organisers and hosts. Shared remembrance and discussion of history helped build understanding and respect between communities.

items.title: First meeting of founding members
items.description:
On 7 February 2026, the Queensland Chinese Affairs Committee held its first founding members’ meeting at Runcorn Tavern, with representatives from 37 founding associations and businesses invited to attend.

Peter Zhuang introduced the committee’s background and purpose. Liu Jizeng chaired the constitution review and election. Members approved the constitution and elected Peter Zhuang as Chairman, with Chen Fan, Chai Hoe, Alan Chen and Chen Dehua as Vice-Chairs. They also approved the nominations of Lin Hai as Secretary-General and Rebecca Zhang as Treasurer.

The meeting approved membership fees and other arrangements, and agreed to hold the official launch in the third quarter, establishing a foundation for the committee’s operations and community work.

items.name: Universal Education & Multicultural Exchange Association (UEMEA)
items.description:
The Universal Education & Multicultural Exchange Association Inc. (UEMEA) builds friendship and mutual understanding between Australia and international communities through education and cultural exchange.

The association promotes Australian education and organises Australian cultural experiences, cultural exchange programs and performance tours. It provides a platform for students, educators and cultural groups to learn, share and collaborate across borders.

Sunnybank Chamber of Commerce was established in 2012, originated in Sunnybank and remains centered around Sunnybank's neighbouring suburbs.

Sunnybank Chambers of Commerce are the voice of business community to local, State and Federal Governments.
